title: Appoint a food safety supervisor
summary: Learn about the requirements and process for appointing a food safety supervisor (FSS) in your business.
intro:
A food safety supervisor (FSS) is someone who is trained to recognise and prevent food handling risks in your business.

Your FSS will need to be trained by a Registered Training Organisation (RTO). They may be the business owner, manager, a supervisor or an employee.

An FSS must be appointed:
who_can_apply: The business must prepare and sell food that is ready to eat, potentially hazardous (temperature-controlled), and not sold or served in the supplier’s original packaging.
The appointed FSS must have a NSW FSS certificate that is less than 5 years old.
The appointed FSS must not be the FSS for any other food premises.
what_you_need: Choose at least one person to be the FSS for each of your premises.
If the chosen person does not already have a valid NSW FSS certificate, they need to get trained by a Registered Training Organisation (RTO).

how_to_steps.text: Choose at least one person to be the FSS for each of your premises.
If they don’t already have a valid NSW FSS certificate, they need to:

more_info.text: appoint one FSS at each of your premises

faqs.q: What is a food safety supervisor (FSS)?
faqs.a: An FSS is someone trained to recognize and prevent food handling risks in your business.

faqs.q: Who can be appointed as an FSS?
faqs.a: The FSS can be the business owner, manager, a supervisor, or an employee.

faqs.q: How often does an FSS need refresher training?
faqs.a: An FSS must get refresher training from a Registered Training Organisation (RTO) every 5 years.
